name: Ember Pendulum
description: Ember Pendulum is a large volcanic world with a distinctive orbital characteristic: its highly elliptical orbit swings it between scorching proximity to its star and a more temperate distance, causing the volcanic activity to surge and recede like a pendulum's swing. At perihelion, the entire surface becomes a sea of lava, while at aphelion, vast plains of cooling rock form temporary continents of black and ember-orange. The exposed core is visible through a polar vent over a thousand kilometers wide, throbbing with light that intensifies as the planet swings starward.

During the cooling phase, the world takes on an apocalyptic beauty, with vast fields of glowing cracks spreading across the newly formed crust like veins of fire in black skin. The toxic atmosphere thins slightly as temperatures drop, allowing brief windows of improved visibility through which the night sky blazes with the light of the nearby star. Extremophile microbial colonies bloom explosively during the cooling phase, covering newly formed rock in mats of heat-resistant organisms that are consumed when the pendulum swings back toward the furnace.

Five monolithic structures stand at equidistant points around the equator, each one a tapered column of an unknown alloy that survives both the molten and cooling phases without visible damage. The monoliths predate any known presence in this system and emit a harmonic tone that shifts in pitch with the planet's orbital position, as though tracking its pendulum swing. Analysis of the harmonic pattern suggests the monoliths may be measuring or regulating the orbit itself, though the mechanism by which they could influence planetary motion remains theoretical.

The exotic matter found in trace amounts in the cooling-phase crust is believed to be produced by the monoliths' interaction with the volcanic cycle, making Ember Pendulum the only known renewable source of this material. Harvesting must occur during the narrow cooling window, and expeditions must be precisely timed to the orbital cycle. The monoliths' harmonic has been gradually shifting over observed centuries, and current projections suggest the orbit itself may be slowly circularizing, a change that would fundamentally transform the planet and potentially deactivate whatever process produces the exotic matter.
